title: Denmark Makes Medical Cannabis Program Permanent As Italy Even Bans CBD!

content_html_sanitized:
Everyone seems to love Denmark. It is certainly one of the most civilized countries in the world. And also a bit eccentric.

Recently, the Danish government finally announced that it was making its medical cannabis program permanent, but as Business of Cannabis reported, “First announced in November 2024, the medical cannabis bill (L135) has undergone an extensive consultation process, with Danish operators united in their calls to amend what’s described as a ‘ludicrous’ reimbursement system, alongside other major hurdles for domestic companies.”

Ironically, until just last year, “recreational” cannabis had been sold openly in Christiania, the old hippie “commune”, since 1971.

Note, 1971 was a year before “The Mellow Yellow Tea House”, founded in Amsterdam by my old friend, Wernerd Bruining, started selling hash through a “house dealer” and four years before The Bulldog “Coffee Shop” started selling cannabis over the counter in December of 1975 in Amsterdam.

But cannabis sales were only allowed in Christiania, and, unlike The Netherlands, there was no regulation. Hyper local anarchy is not a policy.

Amsterdam is a little over 600 kilometers down the North Sea Coast from Copenhagen, and culturally similar, socially tolerant, Protestant, and outward looking.

The Dutch experience has obviously been successful, plus The Netherlands has had both an informal medical program, MediWiet, started decades ago by a group of CoffeeShops in Amsterdam and Haarlem, and there has been formal medical access, covered by the National Health insurance since 2003. Meanwhile, Wernerd Bruining is now focused on CBD, with his  MediWiet foundation,

But, like most of the world, Denmark seems not to have heard about it.

Meanwhile, there is no correlation between national cannabis laws and cannabis consumption in Europe. On the contrary. The top five countries are all Prohibitionist.

The Netherlands ranks sixth, while Italy, which ranks second in use, has even outlawed CBD.

The new law is bizarre. “The text includes the controversial article 18, which prohibits the importation, production, transformation, distribution, commercialization and delivery of Cannabis sativa L. inflorescences, including CBD flowers, CBD resins and CBD oils, regardless of their compliance with legal THC limits. The decree will enter into force imminently after its official publication, as Meloni has activated Article 77 of the Constitution to approve it by urgent means, bypassing parliamentary debate.”

And if you are still not confused enough, in Schleswig-Holstein, the German state just south of Denmark, the state Medical Association has called for “the partial legalization of cannabis to be withdrawn.”

“The number of prescriptions had risen sharply and imports had quadrupled within a year. Medical Association President Henrik Herrmann is calling for a ban on advertising and mandatory doctor-patient contact before prescribing.”

So the state’s organized medical profession, which ignored the medical value of cannabis, is now demanding the authority to decide whether someone is allowed to use it.

Meanwhile, France Making An Even Bigger Mess of Its Cannabis Policy, But Finally About to Legalize Medical After Only Thirty Years

This is “medical science”??? What year in medical school do they teach you how not to be embarrassed?
